articles.title: The Dev Who Accidentally Deleted His Company — The GitLab 2017 Database Incident
articles.excerpt: On 31 January 2017, a tired GitLab SRE typed the wrong hostname and ran rm -rf on 300 GB of production PostgreSQL data. Five backup systems all failed. Here's what happened, why every backup failed, and the disaster recovery lessons every DevOps engineer must learn.

articles.title: One Typo Took Down Facebook for 6 Hours — The 2021 BGP Outage
articles.excerpt: On 4 October 2021, a single bad BGP configuration command withdrew Facebook's DNS prefixes from the internet's routing table. Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp and Oculus vanished for nearly six hours — and engineers were locked out of their own data centers. The networking story every CCNA candidate should know.

articles.title: 11 Lines of Code Broke the Internet — The npm left-pad Incident
articles.excerpt: In 2016, a developer un-published an 11-line npm package called left-pad and broke builds at Facebook, Netflix, Airbnb and thousands of other companies. Here's what happened, why it mattered, and the DevOps lessons that still apply today.
